name: Dashium
description: Sodium-class rendering for Geometry Dash: forced low detail mode, no glow, no particle or shader effects, frozen object animations and batched/culled level sprites.

enabled.name: Enable batching
enabled.description: Collapse level object sprites into as few draw calls as the texture order allows.

cull-offscreen.name: Cull off-screen quads
cull-offscreen.description: Reject quads whose baked vertices fall completely outside the viewport.

show-hud.name: Show stats overlay
show-hud.description: Display quads, draw calls, batch ratio and culled object count in the top-left corner.

force-ldm.name: Force Low Detail Mode
force-ldm.description: Skip decorative 'high detail' objects when a level is loaded. This is the biggest single win in object-heavy levels; turn it off if you want the level to look exactly as authored.

no-glow.name: Disable object glow
no-glow.description: Skip the huge additive glow quads drawn behind glowing objects. Removes most of the fill-rate cost of glow-heavy levels.

orb-effects.name: Disable orb effects & pulse
orb-effects.description: Skip the ring/orb activation burst and stop the looping pulse animation on orbs and rings.

object-animations.name: Disable object animations
object-animations.description: Freeze the looping frame/scale animations on level objects (decorative sprites, pulsing objects, ...). Trigger effects still play; this only removes constant background animation.

effect-layers.name: Disable particle effects
effect-layers.description: Hide particle systems inside the gameplay layer (fire, spawn bursts, ambient effects). Big win in effect-heavy levels. The player's own trail is kept.

shader-effects.name: Disable level shader effects
shader-effects.description: Stop the level's shader objects (shock waves, glitch, lens, blur, ...) from updating. These screen-wide effects are the most expensive thing in 3D-style levels.

max-quads.name: Quads per batch
max-quads.description: Upper bound on how many quads are buffered before a forced flush. Higher means fewer draw calls and more memory traffic.
